phrases.label: Come closer.
Let me take you back.
This story starts with a window
and a fight for the view.
Back when the web was young,
two giants fought to frame the view
Netscape faced Explorer
for the window we looked through
Netscape opened up its code,
let more hands inside the frame.
Mozilla kept the work alive,
then Firefox stepped into the game.
Add a button, block the track,
and make the browser fit your day.
Look beneath the painted surface,
change the way the pieces play.
More eyes checking all the wiring,
more hands working at the seams.
The doorway had a handle on our side of the screen.
Who owns your doorway?
Who decides what you can see?
Let me look, let me change it
Leave the final say with me

scenes.title: Source opens · Firefox arrives
scenes.description: 1998 source release, more hands contributing, and Firefox in 2004. Full-body dancer performs alongside browser props.

scenes.title: Browser workshop
scenes.description: Customize a browser, stop a tracking signal, then use Inspect to change its visible style.

scenes.title: Our side of the doorway
scenes.description: Our handle opens onto nature, architecture and a digital world. A purposeful push ends in an illustrative matched cut, not a geometric morph.

views.name: Door opens onto a connected world

scenes.title: The final say
scenes.description: Return to the same editable browser controls; the user keeps the final choice.

scenes.title: Inside the feed
scenes.description: Pauses and saves form an inferred profile; ranked content moves while user follow/mute controls remain visible.

scenes.title: Make a workshop page
scenes.description: Selected notes and rules enter external model context; a proposed page returns through checks. Publish waits for user approval.

scenes.title: Keep the correction
scenes.description: A user correction is saved outside the unchanged model. The next project loads it; memory and tool permissions remain user-editable.

scenes.title: Show the plan · let me choose
scenes.description: The harness reveals notes, model connection and tool permissions. Approval remains separate from a proposed action.

scenes.title: Who owns the toaster?
scenes.description: Match cut from external intelligence supply to external electricity supply. The narrator turns the dial; notes and tools stay on the user side.

scenes.title: Same question · a new machine
scenes.description: Browser, feed, harness and toaster become four doors. The narrator holds the handle; final lyric is held without rapid word flashes.

scenes.title: Keep the work with me
scenes.description: Music-only closing tableau. The narrator settles; the four story objects continue subtle motion before the final held title.
